text: In Maturana and Varela's theory, a system qualifies as autopoietic if:
choices: It can reproduce and pass genetic material on to offspring
Its components continuously produce and regenerate the very network of processes that produce those components
It grows by accreting material from its environment, the way a crystal does
It maintains a stable internal temperature through negative feedback
explanation: Autopoiesis (from autos, self, and poiein, to make) is defined as self-production: a closed network of processes that regenerates its own components. This definition deliberately excludes viruses (which need host machinery) and crystals (which grow by accretion), and reproduction is a consequence of, not the criterion for, being alive. Thermoregulation is homeostasis, not self-production.
